content: Do not take captopril if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking captopril, contact your doctor immediately. Captopril is prescribed to treat high blood pressure and heart failure. It works by reducing certain chemicals that constrict blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and enabling the heart to pump blood more efficiently. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Captopril is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken two or three times daily on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after a meal. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take captopril exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Captopril helps control high blood pressure and heart failure but does not cure them. Continue taking captopril even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking captopril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to captopril or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially diuretics (water pills), lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), other blood pressure medications, potassium supplements, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had heart or kidney disease or diabetes. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking captopril. Consult your doctor before using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of captopril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Captopril may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience dizziness, lightheadedness, a salty or metallic taste, decreased ability to taste, cough, sore throat, fever, mouth sores, unusual bruising, a fast heartbeat, or excessive tiredness. If any of these symptoms are severe or persistent, contact your doctor. If you experience severe side effects such as chest pain, swelling of the face, eyes, lips, tongue, arms, or legs, difficulty breathing or swallowing, fainting, or a rash, call your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store captopril in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular blood pressure monitoring to assess your response to captopril. Note that captopril tablets may have a slight sulfur odor, similar to rotten eggs. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Patients should be aware that excessive sweating or dehydration can lead to a significant drop in blood pressure due to reduced fluid volume. Other causes of volume depletion, such as vomiting or diarrhea, may also result in a drop in blood pressure. Consult your physician if these occur. Avoid using potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes without consulting your doctor. Patients should not interrupt or discontinue captopril therapy unless instructed by their physician. Those with heart failure should avoid rapid increases in physical activity. Captopril should be taken one hour before meals. Women of childbearing age should be informed about the risks of captopril exposure during pregnancy. Discuss treatment options with women planning to become pregnant, and advise them to report pregnancies to their physicians as soon as possible.
